followup_rationale: No public follow-up is proposed. An explicit failing calibration or a least-dimension result could matter, but this review supplies no concrete construction or sufficiently supported conjecture to justify listing either at the requested high bar.
key_boundaries: The nonrepresentability theorem for normalized complex separable states is Fawzi’s established result. The paper applies that theorem; it does not prove a new quantum-state nonrepresentability theorem.
The two hyperplane equations are imposed inside the oriented mass ball. They alone do not characterize separable states, and Q is only required to be nonnegative on the selected Kähler face.

The failing calibration is existential. No coefficient list, exact comass, explicit separating certificate or rational normalized calibration is supplied. The classical Kähler form used to expose the face is not the failing form.

The counterexample occurs at (k,n) = (4,12). No claim is made that this is the least dimension, that lower-dimensional cases fail, or that earlier experiments in dimensions at most seven were incorrect.

The relevant SOS polynomials have degree at most one, including constants, and equality is taken modulo the full real vanishing ideal. Earlier obstructions for homogeneous quadratic Grassmann cones concern a different representation and do not by themselves establish this oriented mass-ball claim.

Earlier work already supplied the Kähler-face geometry, fermionic projector body, tensor-to-wedge lemma and SOS/completion connection. The claimed addition is their explicit assembly with Fawzi’s obstruction. This bounded comparison does not establish worldwide first priority, formal verification or completed human peer review.
primary_source_review_limitations: The decisive Fawzi theorem was checked at its normalized-complex-state/projected-lift interface, not fully reproved.
